Subject: Security exhibit & pen test logistics for draft MSA

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for sending the draft MSA and order form. Our security team has one blocking item before procurement can sign: we need to confirm the security exhibit language around audit rights and the timing/cadence for delivering evidence (SOC 2, pen-test reports, and any recurring artifact syncs).

High-level asks from Oaken:
- Confirmation of Redwood's SOC 2 attestation and how we can access the report (we typically require a downloadable PDF + readiness to discuss scope).
- Pen test window options and whether our vendor can be granted staging access for a 5-business-day window (we prefer mid-May).
- Proposed cadence for evidence handoff (we prefer weekly rotation for checklist items and a single consolidated packet for monthly artifacts).

I've attached our security questionnaire (partial) for any fields you want to pre-fill; procurement will use that when we finalize the order form. Can you share a proposed evidence rotation schedule and any limitations on pen-test access (e.g., IP allowlists, credentialing, scope exclusions)?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Lee
Security Operations
Oaken Biotech

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed plan below; copying Marissa (legal) and Karthik (security/compliance) so we can lock timing and any redlines to the security exhibit in the MSA/order form.

1) SOC 2: Redwood holds a Type II SOC 2 attestation covering our inference platform controls (security, availability, confidentiality). You can download the report here: https://redwood-inference.example/soc2-report/2026. If you need an NDA'd copy with detailed control mappings, legal can produce that within 2 business days.

2) Pen test window: We can accommodate a staging-only pen test window. Proposed default: May 17–21 (Mon–Fri). Requirements:
  - Staging environment only (no production creds)
  - Requests must come from an approved vendor and IP ranges added to an allowlist 48 hours before testing
  - No social engineering or physical tests allowed

3) Evidence cadence: We typically operate a lightweight weekly evidence rotation for live checklist items (tickets, updated configs, CVE triage status) and a monthly consolidated packet for artifacts (SOC 2, change logs, pen test executive summary). Suggested schedule: weekly handoff on Mondays (artifact list attached) + monthly packet on the 1st of each month.

Next steps (proposed):
- Karhik/Legal to confirm any required redlines to the security exhibit by EOD Monday 4/12.
- Oaken to confirm the pen-test vendor and sign the staging access annex by 4/15.
- I will draft the evidence-rotation cadence into the order form as an exhibit and circulate for signatures.

If you'd prefer a short 30-min call to finalize windows, I'm available Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few guardrails from security/legal that I'll confirm for the exhibit redline:

- Pen test scope: we will limit to non-production staging mirrors that contain synthetic data only. We'll provide a dedicated staging cluster with snapshots and a short lived set of credentials. Live KV caches and customer PII will not be exposed.
- Access model: vendor IP allowlist + time-boxed SSH/API creds that are revoked automatically after the window. We'll ask for a single point-of-contact on Oaken's side for any escalations.
- Evidence handoff: weekly CSV manifests (tickets closed, config checks, patch dates) + monthly ZIP containing higher-level artifacts (SOC 2, change logs, pen test exec summary). The weekly CSV should be uploaded to a secure S3 bucket we will provision; we can also push a Drive link if you prefer.
- Audit rights language: Legal prefers a narrow inspection right limited to evidence exchange and not broad on-site inspection. Marissa, can your team propose a short paragraph to add to the security exhibit that preserves Redwood's operational constraints?

Hannah — if Oaken's vendor needs any special kernel-level access or custom tooling, flag that now; we typically don't grant kernel or hypervisor level testing in staging.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
